scope.purpose: Research dossiers and executable prompt-candidate knowledge only. This artifact neither changes nor proposes safety, filtering, negative-prompt, retry, or age-routing policy.

evidence_classes.source_supported: A factual statement directly bounded by one or more exact source IDs.
evidence_classes.cross_source_synthesis: A conservative combination of source-supported facts; not itself a finding reported verbatim by one source.
evidence_classes.design_inference: A prompt or composition operation derived for illustration; not presented as an empirical attraction finding.
evidence_classes.cultural_record: A dated record of terminology or fan interpretation; not evidence of anatomy, prevalence, causality, or universal preference.

claim_discipline.appeal_boundary: Every appeal mechanism below is a conditional account of why a requested treatment may work for some viewers or briefs. No dossier claims universal attraction, health, morality, personality, gender, age, or diagnosis from appearance.
claim_discipline.still_image_boundary: A single frame can prove only visible geometry, contact, occlusion, material, lighting, and an immediately legible action state. Habit, motive, relationship history, ability, health, and temporal change require other evidence or remain unclaimed.
claim_discipline.candidate_rule: Candidate prompt operations must create observable evidence, not merely repeat the element label.

sources.title: [모에리뷰] Thigh gap 편[2]

sources.title: [모에리뷰] 겨드랑이편

sources.title: [모에리뷰] 포니테일에 대한 잡담.jpg

sources.does_not_support: Does not specify a single visible surface response for every body or pose.

sources.title: Reference Data on the Normal Abdominal Wall Anatomy and Baseline Characteristics in Seventy-One Nulliparous Women

sources.does_not_support: Population and clinical context do not generalize to all bodies or aesthetic preference.

research_questions: Which front/side and assisted/unassisted split-balance distinctions change the visible I-shaped evidence?
Which support-foot, pelvis, and camera choices preserve a continuous vertical chain without perspective distortion?
Which hand, crop, and format resources make the pose incompatible with other requested elements?
How can affect and styling vary without being mistaken for evidence of actual flexibility, training, or health?

definition_and_history.definition: A vernacular image/pose label for a one-leg balance in which the planted support leg, torso, and highly elevated straight free leg read as an approximately vertical I-like silhouette. The FIG technical neighborhood is a front or side split balance, with or without help; I-balance is not used here as an official FIG difficulty name.
definition_and_history.history: The Korean cultural record dated 2020 describes renewed circulation of the I字バランス label in Japanese social illustration, explicitly says the pose and older images pre-existed the trend, and says the first initiator was unknown. The dossier therefore records a 2020 naming/circulation episode, not an origin claim.
terminology_notes: I자 밸런스 and I字バランス are routing aliases for the vernacular silhouette.
Standing split is a broader English description and may include diagonal, front, side, back, assisted, and unassisted balances.
Y-balance is not automatically equivalent: a visibly diagonal free leg and widely branching arms read as Y rather than the requested nearly collinear I.

semantic_subtypes.definition: Support leg vertical under the pelvis; free leg abducted to the side and held near vertical by a hand at the ankle or foot.
distinguishing_evidence: free leg rises laterally beside the torso/head

semantic_subtypes.definition: Support leg vertical; the free leg rises in front of the torso and is held near vertical, best read in a three-quarter view that preserves front-versus-side orientation.
distinguishing_evidence: free thigh originates forward from the pelvis rather than sideways
foreshortening controlled so the free leg remains continuous

semantic_subtypes.definition: The free leg is held near vertical without a hand gripping it, leaving the arms available for balance or expression. It remains an I-balance candidate only when the body and free leg still read nearly collinear.
distinguishing_evidence: no hand supports the free leg
arms visibly counterbalance without creating a second support

semantic_subtypes.definition: An orthogonal execution axis: the support is either a fully planted foot for maximum visual stability or a raised heel/relevé for a narrower, more precarious base.
distinguishing_evidence: support heel visibly down or visibly raised
body center remains over the same support footprint

appeal_mechanisms.description: Compressing a complex human pose into one dominant vertical stroke can make the requested motif immediately legible at thumbnail size.
appeal_mechanisms.non_universal_boundary: Legibility is not attraction; viewers may prefer or reject the extreme silhouette.

appeal_mechanisms.description: A tiny one-foot base plus a high free leg exposes the balancing problem, letting the image communicate a demanding action without caption text.
appeal_mechanisms.non_universal_boundary: The drawing cannot prove actual ability, training, effort, or joint health.

appeal_mechanisms.description: A calm, matter-of-fact, proud, or lightly strained face can create different readings against the same demanding pose; the contrast is selectable rather than inherent.
appeal_mechanisms.non_universal_boundary: No affect is assumed from the pose and no one affect is more appealing to all viewers.

appeal_mechanisms.description: The nearly collinear body/leg chain can organize a vertical poster or character card with a strong top-to-bottom rhythm.
appeal_mechanisms.non_universal_boundary: This is a format advantage, not an attractiveness claim.

Select front split geometry and a three-quarter camera that shows pelvic orientation.
Reserve one hand and require visible hand-to-ankle/foot contact.
Keep both hands away from the free leg and use arms as visible counterbalance.
Show heel and forefoot on one continuous ground plane.
Show a raised heel and smaller base while preserving vertical center-over-foot alignment.
Prioritize near-collinearity, full-body visibility, and low perspective distortion.
Allow a modest angle while retaining one-foot balance; do not call a clearly diagonal Y-pose a strict I.
Use relaxed brows and controlled gaze without erasing the pose geometry.
Use direct gaze or small confident smile and open free arm.
Use focused gaze and subtle stabilizing tension, not anatomically broken joints.

Abduct the free leg laterally until it runs nearly vertical beside the torso and head.
Place the same-side hand around the ankle or foot with unbroken fingers and a visible contact boundary.
Keep pelvis, thigh, knee, shin, ankle, and foot continuous; show the ground shadow under only the support foot.
observable_evidence_groups: head and both feet inside frame
candidate_realizations.camera: Level frontal camera, moderate distance, minimal wide-angle expansion; portrait 2:3 or 3:4.

candidate_realizations.prompt_operation_en: Turn the pelvis three-quarters and raise the forward free leg near vertical, supporting its ankle while preserving the planted foot and leg-to-torso separation.
prompt_operations: Turn the torso and pelvis three-quarters to camera so the free thigh is visibly forward rather than lateral.
Raise the front free leg near vertical and support it at ankle/foot with one hand.
Separate the near and far contours with lighting so the leg does not merge into the torso.
Keep the support foot fully visible and centered under the body's projected mass.
candidate_realizations.camera: Three-quarter full body at pelvis height or slightly above; avoid a close low angle that enlarges the near leg.

candidate_realizations.prompt_operation_en: Hold one free leg near vertical without hand contact and use asymmetrical arms to counterbalance over one visible support foot.
prompt_operations: Hold the free leg near vertical without either hand touching it.
Use the arms asymmetrically as counterbalance, keeping them away from the mouth and free-leg contact zone.
Show a narrow one-foot base and subtle torso correction without collapsing the waist or hip joint.
Preserve the I-like silhouette even though the arms branch from it.
candidate_realizations.camera: Frontal or slight three-quarter full body; vertical frame with clear lateral breathing room for the arms.

candidate_realizations.prompt_operation_en: Render an assisted near-vertical side split on a raised support heel as a clean high-contrast full-body poster silhouette with one forefoot shadow.
prompt_operations: Use an assisted side split on a visibly raised support heel.
Place the figure against a simple high-contrast background so the full vertical contour owns its borders.
Keep clothing and hair subordinate to the I contour; allow a ponytail to trail laterally only if requested.
Retain one small contact shadow below the forefoot rather than floating the figure.
candidate_realizations.camera: Orthographic-feeling frontal poster view, moderate/long virtual focal length, portrait format.

pose: Exactly one support foot contacts the ground; the free leg must not acquire a second hidden support.
Knee direction, ankle, foot, and pelvis must form one plausible continuous chain.
Assisted variants reserve one hand for a visible ankle/foot contact; unassisted variants reserve arm space for counterbalance.
A strict I candidate requires a near-vertical free leg. A visibly diagonal split must be routed as a softer vertical or a different balance, not mislabeled.
camera: Full-body crop is mandatory for direct evidence because the support foot, free foot, head, and ground contact all matter.
Prefer a level frontal or three-quarter camera at moderate distance. Close wide-angle or steep low-angle views can enlarge the near limb and obscure joint continuity.
Leave margin above the raised foot and below the support foot; cropping either destroys the primary evidence.
format: Portrait 2:3, 3:4, or vertical card is native.
Square is viable only with a smaller full-body figure and simplified background.
Wide banner is a soft conflict; fallback to a vertical inset, paired panel, or choose another requested element as primary rather than bending the leg diagonally just to fill width.

resources.hands: one reserved in assisted variants; both free but compositionally active in unassisted variants

synergies.reason: A laterally lagging tail can counterbalance the dominant vertical stroke without consuming a hand if already tied.
synergies.rule: Keep the tie point and bundle visible and secondary to the pose.

synergies.reason: Static glasses add face detail without consuming leg or hand resources.
synergies.rule: Do not require an adjustment gesture in the assisted variant.

synergies.reason: The long torso-pelvis chain can show stretch/tension as a support detail.
synergies.rule: Accept reduced abdomen detail in a full-body frame; do not crop out the support foot to enlarge it.

hard_conflicts.reason: The direct thigh-gap proof requires both feet together/near together, while I-balance requires one free foot elevated.
hard_conflicts.fallback: Use paired frames or choose one element as primary; never claim both from the same single pose.

soft_conflicts.reason: Finger-to-mouth needs a close crop and a hand at the mouth; I-balance needs full-body evidence and may reserve that hand for leg support.
soft_conflicts.fallback: Use an unassisted balance only if a full-body hand-to-mouth gesture remains legible, otherwise paired frames.

soft_conflicts.reason: Both demand extreme limb placement and clear shoulder/hip chains, increasing anatomy and visibility load.
soft_conflicts.fallback: Use one raised free arm in an unassisted pose, or let axilla remain incidental rather than primary.

soft_conflicts.reason: Phone/mirror geometry and hand use compete with balance proof and a stable frontal silhouette.
soft_conflicts.fallback: Remote camera/tripod or paired view; do not invent an unseen photographer relationship.

source_supported_claims.claim: FIG distinguishes front and side split balances and variants with or without help.
One-foot balances involve control of the body over a small base of support; measured rhythmic-gymnastics studies use center-of-pressure and ground-reaction data.
The 2020 Korean record describes I字バランス as a newly circulating label for an older pose and leaves the first origin unknown.

cross_source_synthesis: Treat the fan label as an iconic rendering of a technically broader family of split balances; route front/side and assisted/unassisted as independent choices.
The most reliable single-frame proof is not an anatomical angle number but a visible one-foot base, continuous free leg, optional contact, and uncropped vertical silhouette.
design_inference: Use a moderate-distance, level full-body view as the neutral candidate because camera-induced limb distortion is a known risk and the I motif depends on relative alignment.
Use affect as an independent preference axis; the pose itself does not prove pride, ease, pain, or skill.
limitations: The vernacular meme origin and first creator remain unverified.
A still image cannot prove flexibility, balance ability, training, difficulty, safety, joint range, pain, or health.
FIG rules describe sport execution, not fan-art meaning, and the two-case biomechanics study is not normative.
Exact joint angles should not be inferred from a stylized drawing.
No source establishes this pose as universally attractive.

labels.ja: サイギャップ·絶対空域

research_questions: What stance and contour evidence distinguishes a feet-together thigh gap from ordinary space created by a wide stance?
How do camera perspective, pelvis rotation, clothing, and background alter the apparent negative space?
How can width and garment preferences be routed without turning the element into a body-size, health, or beauty metric?
Which full-body visibility resources conflict with close-up facial or action elements?

definition_and_history.definition: A visible region of background between the medial thighs when the character stands upright with knees straight and feet touching or nearly touching. This dossier treats it as a stance-dependent negative-space relation, not as a body-size, health, or value metric.
definition_and_history.history: An informal English lexicographic record places broad public/social-media visibility in the early 2010s while noting earlier scattered uses. A Korean fan-cultural record discussed the motif in 2019. The exact first use and Japanese 絶対空域 lineage are not independently established here.
terminology_notes: 허벅지 틈 and thigh gap are direct descriptive aliases.
사이 갭 is a Korean transliteration of the English phrase.
絶対空域 is a fan-cultural pun/alias and must not be confused with 絶対領域, the stocking-to-skirt exposed-thigh zone.
A gap created only by a wide stance is not the feet-together thigh-gap construction.

semantic_subtypes.definition: A small continuous background opening that remains visible with feet together without deleting or pinching the inner-thigh contours.
distinguishing_evidence: knees and lower legs remain distinct

semantic_subtypes.definition: A larger but still anatomically continuous opening, rendered as one coherent patch of background rather than a cutout or missing anatomy.
distinguishing_evidence: inner thighs taper naturally toward knees
no duplicated or erased leg segments

semantic_subtypes.definition: Shorts, a short skirt, leotard, stockings, or tights establish an upper boundary or material contrast while the actual inner-thigh negative space remains visible.
distinguishing_evidence: background remains visible below/inside the boundary
garment does not paint a false skin-colored hole
leg continuity through knee and foot

semantic_subtypes.definition: A high-contrast, simplified full-body treatment in which the negative space is intentionally legible as a shape while surrounding body features remain sufficient to avoid turning it into a body-size symbol.
distinguishing_evidence: complete outer and inner leg contours

appeal_mechanisms.description: A background region bounded by two medial contours can become a crisp figure-ground cue, making the requested feature readable without outlining or labeling it.
appeal_mechanisms.non_universal_boundary: Perceptual clarity is not evidence of aesthetic preference.

appeal_mechanisms.description: The inward and outward curves of two complete legs can create a repeated contour rhythm whose width and softness are adjustable to the user's brief.
appeal_mechanisms.non_universal_boundary: Curvature preference is heterogeneous and context-dependent; no thigh contour is universally preferred.

appeal_mechanisms.description: A hem, piping line, stocking top, or tights material can frame the negative space and make clothing structure participate in the motif.
appeal_mechanisms.non_universal_boundary: This is a compositional option, not a claim about modesty or attraction.

appeal_mechanisms.description: The gap can route attention to the lower-body region, but experiments indicate body-size judgments integrate multiple lower-body features rather than relying on one gap alone.
appeal_mechanisms.non_universal_boundary: The feature must never be described as a sufficient sign of body size, health, weight, fitness, or value.

values.selection_effect: Select a small continuous opening and prioritize natural contour continuity.
Select a clearly visible but non-exaggerated opening.
Increase negative-space width only while preserving complete legs and the feet-together proof; mark as stylized if needed.
Require both full feet touching or nearly touching on one ground plane.
Allow small foot-angle variation but reject a wide stance as proof.
Use skin/background edge contrast with no hosiery material boundary.
Keep both curved hems and inner-thigh opening visible.
Use coherent hosiery coverage and let the gap show background rather than skin-colored fill.
Show the garment's lower boundary without occluding the medial-thigh opening.
Use the neutral direct-evidence candidate.
Allow slight rotation only if both medial contours and feet remain readable.
Treat as stylized; reduce reliability and never infer anatomy or natural width from it.
Place an uncluttered contrasting field behind the legs.
Keep a locally quiet patch of background inside the gap even in a detailed scene.

candidate_realizations.prompt_operation_en: Place both complete feet together in a neutral frontal stance and preserve a small continuous background opening between two complete medial-thigh contours.
prompt_operations: Place both complete feet touching or nearly touching on one ground plane in a neutral frontal stance.
Preserve two full thighs and knees while leaving a small continuous patch of background between the medial thighs.
Use soft even lighting so the opening is not confused with a deep painted shadow.
Keep hips, knees, lower legs, and feet inside frame.
observable_evidence_groups: two complete lower legs and feet
candidate_realizations.camera: Level frontal full-body or knees-to-feet only when hip/stance context remains visible; moderate distance.

candidate_realizations.prompt_operation_en: Keep strict feet-together frontal proof while widening the real background opening without deleting, spiking, or shadow-faking either inner thigh contour.
prompt_operations: Use the same strict feet-together proof as the neutral candidate.
Increase the visible background opening without narrowing thighs into spikes or deleting inner contours.
Retain outer-thigh and hip context so the gap is not the only body-size cue.
Use a simple background color distinct from skin and garment values.
observable_evidence_groups: complete medial and outer thigh contours
candidate_realizations.camera: Frontal, level, full lower body with moderate/long virtual focal length.

candidate_realizations.prompt_operation_en: Frame the medial-thigh background opening with coherent curved shorts hems while keeping both thighs separate and both feet together inside the frame.
prompt_operations: Place symmetric or intentionally asymmetric shorts hems above the medial-thigh opening.
Keep cloth piping, side slit, or curved hem coherent with the garment construction.
Show a locally quiet background through the actual gap and both complete feet together.
Prevent the shorts from merging the two thighs into one central shape.
candidate_realizations.camera: Frontal full body or head-to-feet character card; do not crop the feet.

candidate_realizations.prompt_operation_en: Use coherent matching hosiery and a flat contrasting background so the genuine feet-together opening reads as background rather than skin-colored fill.
prompt_operations: Use coherent matching hosiery on both legs and a flat contrasting background.
Let the background, not a skin-tone patch, define the opening.
Preserve material transparency, seam, or stocking-top logic only if requested.
Keep both legs, knees, and feet anatomically continuous.
observable_evidence_groups: coherent hosiery material on both legs
candidate_realizations.camera: Orthographic-feeling frontal poster/card composition.

pose: Both feet and knees must be together or nearly together; a wide stance produces ordinary inter-leg space, not direct thigh-gap evidence.
Both thighs, knees, shins, and feet remain complete. Never create the gap by erasing anatomy or merging a skin-colored mask into the background.
Pelvis rotation should be small enough that both medial contours remain visible for the neutral definition.
camera: Frontal and level is the evidence-maximizing baseline.
Close wide-angle and low-angle views can change apparent limb proportions; route those only when explicitly requested and mark them stylized.
A crop above the feet cannot prove the defining stance; a crop below the hips can also conceal ordinary wide stance.
format: Portrait or character card supports complete stance evidence.
Square works with a centered full-body figure and restrained environment.
Horizontal banner is a soft conflict; use a full-body inset or a second environmental subject rather than widening the stance.

contacts: two feet on same ground plane

definition_and_history.definition: A deliberately posed, explicitly adult character has a thumb or finger pad visibly sealed by or shallowly inside the lips. This is a single-frame contact state, not evidence of a recurring habit, emotional cause, diagnosis, relationship, or age regression.
definition_and_history.history: A dated 2018 Korean fan-cultural article records 손가락을 빠는 행동 as a discussed illustration motif. definition_and_history.definition: A paired-lens optical face accessory consisting, depending on construction, of lenses, bridge, rims or mounting points, and temples that contact the nose and ears. definition_and_history.history: The College of Optometrists traces rivet spectacles to the thirteenth century, later bridge forms and eighteenth-century temple glasses, and twentieth-century diversification into fashion. terminology_notes: 테안경/full-rim means each lens is enclosed by a visible rim.

무테/rimless mounts lenses at discrete bridge/temple points and still requires bridge plus temple attachments.

definition_and_history.definition: A hairstyle in which scalp hair converges into one primary gather/tie point, then hangs or moves as a single tail-like bundle whose envelope is shaped by fiber properties, gravity, compression, and motion.
definition_and_history.history: Kotobank defines the Japanese term by hair gathered at the back and hanging like a pony's tail, records a Japanese textual example from 1956-57, and places fashion circulation in the 1950s. A 2017 Korean fan-cultural article records high, low, side, motion, nape, and re-tying variants; this is terminology history, not a claim of first global invention.
terminology_notes: 높은 포니테일/high ponytail places the single gather above the occipital midline; 로우 포니테일/low ponytail places it near the nape.
사이드 포니테일/side ponytail shifts one gather point laterally; two symmetric gather points are twintails, not one ponytail.
땋은 포니테일/braided ponytail keeps one tied base and then organizes the tail into a braid.
묶는 중/re-tying is an action state requiring both hands, loose upstream hair, and one intended gather target.
포니테일의 흔들림/motion means a displaced bundle with causal lag/follow-through, not an arbitrary sideways rigid rod.

semantic_subtypes.definition: One gather point sits high on the back of the head, with an elevated root and a tail that arcs outward before gravity turns it downward.

One gather point is deliberately lateral on the head, and one tail emerges on that side; the opposite side must not gain a second matching tail.
Hair first converges at one tie point and the downstream bundle is braided; the tied base distinguishes it from a braid beginning directly at the scalp.
Both hands gather loose hair toward one target and a tie is visible before or during closure; the hairstyle is communicated as an action rather than a completed static state.

definition_and_history.definition: The visible anterior and anterolateral torso region between the lower rib margin and pelvis, treated as a continuous, pose-responsive surface. Candidate states include neutral softness, stretch, twist-related tension/compression, seated folds, and optional trained definition; none is a health or identity metric.
definition_and_history.history: A 2017 Korean fan-cultural article discusses the belly/abdomen as a visual preference focus and explicitly records divergent preferences for soft, folded, and defined treatments. Clinical anatomy and recent biomechanics describe a layered abdominal wall with meaningful normal variation and deformation across breathing, activation, pressure, and motor tasks.

limitations: A still image cannot measure muscle activation, intra-abdominal pressure, breathing phase, strength, fitness, pain, pregnancy, disease, or body composition.
Surface softness, folds, definition, navel shape, and waist contour vary and do not establish age, gender, ethnicity, diet, activity, health, or morality.
The cited reference-data population does not generalize to all bodies, and clinical internal anatomy does not dictate one visible surface.
The cultural article is subjective and cannot establish prevalence or a superior body type.
No source establishes any abdomen treatment as universally attractive.
